meta: Generated 2026-04-26 · RDKit 2026.03.1 · BaseFeatures.fdef · interaction-filtered · 6 PDB complexes (4× A1E, 2× AGS)
summary_html:
Six ATR protein–ligand complexes were analyzed to derive structure-based pharmacophore queries for virtual screening. Two ligand chemotypes anchor the analysis: A1E, a synthetic inhibitor (9L40, 9L45, 9L4B, 9L4D), and AGS, an ATP analog / adenosine-thiophosphate (9L46, 9L4F).

A1E adopts two distinct binding sub-modes — an ASP2494 / GLY2385 motif and a TYR2365 motif — providing two complementary pharmacophore queries. The receptor engages a conserved set of hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor features; positively-ionizable groups consistently pair with ASP2494.

Key finding for screening: Build queries from Donor and Acceptor features (with PosIonizable as an optional ASP2494 constraint). Aromatic and hydrophobic ligand features never contact the protein across any structure — exclude them. A second, non-productive A1E copy in 9L40 (resnum 2702) retains zero features and serves as a built-in negative control.

modes.name: Primary query · A1E Mode 1 (ASP2494 / GLY2385)
modes.desc: The dominant A1E binding mode. A Donor/PosIonizable pair engages ASP2494 (OD1) while two acceptors hydrogen-bond the GLY2385 backbone amide.
modes.strategy: Screen first. Require 3 of 4 features matched, with the Donor/PosIonizable pair at ASP2494 mandatory (same ligand position).

modes.name: Secondary query · A1E Mode 2 (TYR2365)
modes.desc: An alternate A1E pose anchored on the TYR2365 hydroxyl. Two adjacent donors both donate to the same tyrosine OH (effectively one point with wider tolerance).
modes.strategy: Rescreen top Mode-1 hits. Require Donor → TYR2365; merge the two adjacent donors into one 1.5 Å sphere. Overlap with Mode 1 flags dual-mode ligands.

modes.name: ATP-site filter · AGS
modes.desc: The ATP pocket engages different phosphate oxygens in 9L46 vs 9L4F, so no reproducible cross-structure query emerges. AGS bond orders are high-confidence (CCD template matched).
modes.strategy: Use 9L4F (4 features) as reference and apply a loose partial match (3 of 7) as a selectivity filter to exclude ATP-competitive compounds — not as a primary query.

interaction_map:
ASP2494  ← [Donor] [PosIonizable]      A1E Mode 1 (9L40, 9L45)
GLY2385  ← [Acceptor] [Acceptor]        A1E Mode 1 (9L40, 9L45)
GLU2378  ← [Donor]                       A1E Mode 1 (9L40) + AGS (9L4F)
TYR2365  ← [Donor] [Donor]              A1E Mode 2 (9L4B, 9L4D)
SER2305  ← [Acceptor]                    A1E Mode 2 (9L4D)
VAL2380  ← [Acceptor]                    A1E Mode 2 (9L4D)
PRO2328  ← [Donor] [Acceptor]           AGS (9L4F)
ASP2330  ← [Acceptor]                    AGS (9L4F)
ALA2304  ← [Donor]                       AGS (9L46)
GLU2479  ← [Donor]                       AGS (9L46)
ILE2377  ← [Donor]                       AGS (9L46)
interaction_map_note: GLU2378 appears in both A1E Mode 1 and the AGS ATP-site, suggesting it is a versatile hydrogen-bond partner accessible from different binding poses.

limitations.impact: AssignBondOrdersFromTemplate failed for all A1E structures (smiles_source: template_failed_best_effort); some Donor/Acceptor assignments may be misclassified.
limitations.mitigation: Supply a validated A1E SMILES on re-run; cross-check feature assignments against PyMOL visual inspection of the .pml files.

limitations.impact: 0 retained features despite 17 detected — a crystallographic / non-productive pose.
limitations.mitigation: Use as a negative reference only; exclude from query construction.

limitations.impact: 9L46 and 9L4F engage different phosphate oxygens, so the ATP-site query is not reproducible.
limitations.mitigation: Apply AGS as a selectivity filter rather than a primary query.

limitations.impact: π-stacking or hydrophobic contacts may be under-detected by the simplified protein-side feature lookup.
limitations.mitigation: Add manually if specific π-stacking residues are known to engage the scaffold.
